README: The sound sheet. Music follows the night, not the place: it thins through the grind, cuts to dead silence for the four seconds he loses six hours of work (6.lava → 6.orange), and only comes back when the boy touches his dad's shoulder. Every effect mirrors something on screen — a torch being placed, a tick on each number of the count, one wooden sword hitting last. Silence is used once, and only for the defeat.

sections.why: A man in armour on backwards, pressing one key with one finger. Light, so we laugh with him and not at him.
The catch-22: twelve eyes, and the only way to a pearl is a monster he will not look at.
The flashback. 'Too slow for this game' — the reason he is down a hole at midnight.
The grind: four hundred blocks, one torch every ten, a man working quietly so nobody wakes up.
The bedtime promise, and all the tomorrows that never came.
The dread: the torch finds the lava and the music climbs with the light.
The low point. The music cuts dead on the moment the shaft lights up: six hours of digging, gone in one frame.
One low note and air, while the defeat sinks in. Almost silence, but the film is not dead.
The boy reads the sign and understands what four hundred blocks means. The turn.
He turns round. The bravest thing in the film is a man looking at a cartoon monster.
Twelve eyes at breakfast, together, and the portal opening.
The payoff: he lands the last hit with the sword he made at midnight.

beds.why: His room at midnight: the hum of a computer and nothing else.
Down the shaft: rock, and a long way down.
Back at the desk with the empty grid.
The field at night: crickets, and an enderman standing in it.
The same room, two years earlier.
Four hundred blocks down: close stone and a torch.
The bedroom, years ago, at the edge of the light.
The bottom of the shaft, looking up.
Lava behind the wall: roar and hiss, over the silence where the music was.
Head down on the desk. Almost nothing, so the room is not dead.
Grey light before sunrise, the sign at the top of the hole.
Morning, the same hole, a boy reading it.
Back at the desk where it started.
The end of the night, out in the field.
Morning light, and the open air above the End.
Still morning. The ask goes out over the same air.

sfx.why: The monitor, in the dark: the only light in the room.
Armour on backwards: cloth shifting as he leans over the mouse.
The note taped to the wall: BEAT IT BEFORE HE WAKES.
The dragon on the poster behind him, lit by the monitor.
One block down, and then another: the hole begins.
The camera goes with him: a long fall into the shaft.
The empty grid: twelve slots with nothing in them.
Twelve, and he has none of them. A flat no.
The pearl on the grid, held like an object in a museum.
The enderman: two violet eyes, and a chord that does not resolve.
The macro on the eyes: this is the thing he will not look at.
He turns his head away, one hand up over his eyes.
Not for anything. The catch-22 closes.
Two years ago: a cut back in time.
'Too slow for this game.' The cruellest line in the film, and the reason. A small sound: the voice has to stay on top of it.
The dad in the doorway, hearing it, not letting it show.
He never said he had heard it. The film's whole middle is in that.
Midnight, on the clock on the wall.
The first thing he ever crafted: a wooden sword.
Four hundred blocks: the digging, over and over.
Stone breaking and settling at the bottom of the shaft.
A torch placed on the wall, every ten blocks.
So he would not be scared. He was.
A tick on each number written on the wall.
The count running up the wall as the camera slides past it: 100, 200, 300, 400.
A boy in bed, years ago, asking the question he already knows the answer to.
'Play with me' — the ask, and the ask is small.
'Tomorrow.' The promise breaking, gently, every time.
He was always tired. A man sitting down heavily.
Now he is the one waiting, four hundred blocks down: one drop of water in the dark.
Four in the morning.
The torch finds it: lava light on the shaft wall.
The film's one big sound: six hours of digging, gone in a frame.
The shaft collapsing behind the light.
Six hours of it, remembered in one hit.
Head down on the desk. A soft landing, and then the room.
The sign going into the ground at the top of the hole: SORRY. I TRIED.
And then the house goes quiet.
Morning: feet on the floor, a door.
He reads the sign: Sorry. I tried.
A hand on a shoulder, and the man waking up.
'You don't dig to the End.' The boy is teaching now.
The second before he looks. The enderman is closer than it has ever been.
He turns round. Heavy, slow, and the bravest move in the film.
The enderman, right there, at his height.
He looked. One held beat, and the reward was always for looking.
The pearl on the ground where the enderman was.
Twelve eyes into twelve slots, at breakfast, together.
The portal opens. The grid from the second beat is full at last.
The last hit, with the wooden sword he made at midnight.
The dragon's wing going over.
The dragon breaking into light.
The two of them, in the first gold of morning.
Four hundred blocks, and a dad who has never played.
The subscribe line.
